To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the theoretical and the experimental system identification methods are capable of identifying dynamic models of flexible structure with piezoelectrical transducers (i. e. smart structures); (b) the theoretical and experimental methods produce similar models for the same system; and (c) the experimental method can be used to identify dynamic models of any system.
the Finite Element Method can be used to model the dynamic behavior of smart structures, and the μ synthesis technique can be employed to match a transfer to the FRF of the smart structure.
two different methods were employed to extract the dynamic model of a smart structure, and that the results of both methods agreed with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and experimental verification of control techniques for flexible smart structures.
the development of control algorithms and implementation of these algorithms on a smart structure.
the development of a control system for vibration suppression of flexible structures with embedded piezoelectric actuators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods can be used to identify the dynamic models of any dynamic system and can be applied to the design of control laws for the system.
the theoretical system identification is more accurate and faster than the experimental system identification.
the proposed methodologies can be used to identify a dynamic model of a system with piezoelectrics and can be applied to other systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dynamic system model is required for the control design.
the theoretical and experimental system identification methods are valid for smart structures.
the state space model is the best model to represent the dynamics of smart structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a smart structure is a dynamic system and can be modeled and controlled in the same way as any other system.
a smart structure is no different than a traditional structure from the point of view of modeling and system identification.
the state space model is the preferred model for the control design and the implementation.
